Turn a number's lowest five bits into the actions of a secret handshake, reversed when the fifth bit is set.

Adapted from Exercism's [problem specification](https://github.com/exercism/problem-specifications/tree/main/exercises/secret-handshake) (MIT). Listed under [Numbers & Math](/examples/?subject=numbers-and-math).

```nomi-run
// FILE: secret_handshake.nomi
//# The secret handshake a number's lowest five bits spell.

once reverse_bit = 16

/// An action of the handshake, in the order the bits list them.
pub enum Action {
    Wink
    DoubleBlink
    CloseYourEyes
    Jump
}

derive Variants for Action

/// The actions `number`'s bits ask for: one per set bit from 1 to 8, in that
/// order, reversed when bit 16 is set too. Higher bits are ignored.
pub fn commands(number: Int) -> List<Action> {
    actions =
        Action.variants()
        |> Iter.filter(fn action -> set?(number, bit(action)))
        |> Iter.to_list()

    if set?(number, reverse_bit) {
        Iter.reverse(actions)
    } else {
        actions
    }
}

fn bit(action: Action) -> Int {
    case action {
        .Wink -> 1
        .DoubleBlink -> 2
        .CloseYourEyes -> 4
        .Jump -> 8
    }
}

fn set?(number: Int, bit: Int) -> Bool {
    Int.bitwise_and(number, bit) != 0
}

// FILE: secret_handshake_test.nomi
import {
    secret_handshake
    secret_handshake.Action
}

test "commands" {
    cases = [
        #("wink for 1", 1, [Action.Wink]),
        #("double blink for 10", 2, [.DoubleBlink]),
        #("close your eyes for 100", 4, [.CloseYourEyes]),
        #("jump for 1000", 8, [.Jump]),
        #("combine two actions", 3, [.Wink, .DoubleBlink]),
        #("reverse two actions", 19, [.DoubleBlink, .Wink]),
        #("reversing one action gives the same action", 24, [.Jump]),
        #("reversing no actions still gives no actions", 16, []),
        #("all possible actions", 15, [.Wink, .DoubleBlink, .CloseYourEyes, .Jump]),
        #("reverse all possible actions", 31, [.Jump, .CloseYourEyes, .DoubleBlink, .Wink]),
        #("do nothing for zero", 0, []),
    ]

    subtests cases, #(description, number, expected), description {
        assert secret_handshake.commands(number) == expected
    }
}
```

## How it's written

- Actions are an `Action` enum with `derive Variants`, so `Action.variants()` lists them in bit order, and the canonical strings become variants in the tests.
- Each action's bit is spelled out in a `case` (`bit`), as allergies does, rather than computed from the action's position.
- The reverse flag is a `once reverse_bit = 16`, tested by the same `set?` helper as the actions.
- The filter is `fn action -> set?(number, bit(action))` rather than the capture `&set?(number, bit(&1))`: the body is two calls, and style §31 keeps captures for one.
- The table qualifies only its first row's action (`[Action.Wink]`); the later rows' bare variants, and the empty lists, take that enum.
